summary.intent: Clean up GitHub issue #655's checkbox lists into a proper native sub-issue tree (per a prior recorded plan), and integrate PR #980 onto post-#982 main, then drive it through security/crypto/simplify/CodeRabbit review gates to a ready-to-flip state.
summary.outcome: Both tasks completed: #655 converted to 9 track umbrellas covering all 141 refs (zero orphans) plus #719 got 8 new leaf issues; #980 was integrated, passed 4 review gates (security-review, crypto-privacy-review, simplify, CodeRabbit CLI) with all real findings fixed and 6 follow-up issues filed with verified dependency edges, landing at commit 80867e7f4 (draft, MERGEABLE) awaiting the user's ready-flip while CodeRabbit web review runs. A stale-tooling issue (#973) was fixed via a separate draft PR (#1011), and a CONTEXT.md crypto-glossary inconsistency it surfaced was independently verified and fixed on a new branch.

repo: GitHub's dependency API stores one edge and projects it both ways — a single POST .../dependencies/blocked_by is sufficient, no need to also POST the inverse 'blocking' relation.

SecretBytes (crates/core/src/suite/secret.rs) is deliberately not PartialEq to prevent timing-variable equality on secrets; ct_eq_32 constant-time comparison lives engine-side in crates/engine/src/secret_util.rs, creating a real dependency for any core type wrapping secret equality.
MEDIA_WINDOW_BYTES = 1_048_536 (not 1_048_576) is intentional — it equals ContentProfile::PRODUCTION.chunk_size (1 MiB minus seal overhead), not a typo; main's old 1024*1024 value was the actual bug.

StreamHandle ids are a per-engine counter restarting at 1, so a stale client-side handle can silently alias onto a different engine/leader's stream unless explicitly fenced by leadership change, not just port change.

.claude/commands/crypto-privacy-review.md and .claude/agents/crypto-privacy-reviewer.md both still describe v1 crypto architecture (AES-256-GCM, ECIES, PBKDF2/Argon2, Web Crypto API, TEE hardware IPNS decryption) — fixed in PR #1011, but any unbriefed reviewer agent run before that lands gets the wrong checklist.

CONTEXT.md line 15 said the owner blob is 'ECIES-wrapped to the vault owner's identity key' — both wrong: blueprint/core.md:79 puts it under HPKE base mode, and CONTEXT.md:41 itself states 'the identity key only signs; the subkey only seals', so it should reference the enc subkey.
landing/ directory intentionally still references v1 primitives (AES-GCM, ECIES) as marketing copy for the deployed v1 system — not a target for crypto-doc cleanup.
blueprint/core.md and blueprint/web-client.md contain 'Gone / Killed by' retirement tables listing ECIES etc. as history — correct as-is, must not be edited when hunting stale v1 references.

code.finding: swapCurrent() is the only function that clears EngineClient.streams; only called from installFollower (line 248) and promote (line 308) — a leadership change where this tab stays a follower never triggers it, leaving stale stream handles that alias onto the new leader's engine.

onLeader() drops the port and rejects pending requests on a leadership change but does not clear the stream handle table — root cause of the HIGH stale-handle bug; fixed via a new onLeadershipChange hook.
LiveStreams had no cap or eviction; capped at MAX_OPEN_STREAMS=256 with a fail-closed EngineError::TooManyStreams, checked both before and atomically inside borrow_mut.
cb:portHello accepts any self-asserted clientId string as the port owner — ownership is lifecycle bookkeeping, not authentication, despite a comment claiming port possession authenticates ownership.
read_content_range was believed dead but had a live caller (Engine::read_content with (node,0,u64::MAX)); resolved by making it a private read_whole rather than deleting it outright.

workflow: Sequence review gates by mutation: run read-only gates (security-review, crypto-privacy-review) in parallel first, then writing gates (simplify) alone afterward to avoid analyzing shifting code.

Verify subagent claims independently against the actual remote/code state before relaying them to the user or acting further (e.g. re-checking #980's mergeable state, PR #1011's grep counts, and the write-handle aliasing claim on main).
Hold a CodeRabbit ready-flip until all other gates are green, since re-drafting a PR does not cancel an in-flight web review and the review slot burns on whatever is pushed at that moment.

When filing follow-up issues discovered mid-review, verify the underlying code claim yourself (e.g. reading SecretBytes/ct_eq_32) before adding a dependency edge, rather than trusting the reviewing agent's inference from titles.

For a scoped agent task on a stale-doc issue, do a quick grep survey across related tracked files before briefing, since the issue text may name only one of several stale files (crypto-privacy-review.md issue also implicated the paired .claude/agents/crypto-privacy-reviewer.md).

friction: Bash `read` tool's tab collapsing corrupted rows with no prior parent during the 37-issue reparenting pass, requiring a retry of 10 failed reparentings.
zsh doesn't word-split unquoted variables, breaking bulk gh issue attachment commands until rewritten in Python.

An earlier agent's brief that read_content_range's only callers were two tests was wrong — it had a live production caller (Engine::read_content), caught only because the fix-pass agent verified before deleting.

CodeRabbit CLI raised a 'major' finding (revert MEDIA_WINDOW_BYTES to 1_048_576) that was actually asking to reintroduce the bug the PR fixes; required independent verification against main to reject correctly.

Stale test-count baseline (773) was carried forward from an earlier gate run without re-verification; the simplify-gate agent caught the actual figure (800) by stashing and re-running at the prior commit.
Agent worktree lacked node_modules, so the husky pre-commit hook failed (lint-staged not found), forcing a --no-verify commit after manually running markdownlint/prettier from the main checkout.
